[NLFC.1.1] Creating an engine is the only allocation an integrator has to
make explicitly. Everything else in libds hangs off the handle it returns.

The call takes a configuration ([NLFC.1.2]) and yields the handle through an
**out-parameter**, because the return channel carries the status ([NLFC.7.1]).
Read the handle only once that status says the call succeeded.

What comes back is a complete but empty engine: defaults chosen, no schemas,
no rules, no callbacks registered, clock live ([NLFC.1.4]), and no state
shared with any other engine in the process ([NLFC.1.3]). The caller owns it
from here until teardown ([NLFC.6]).
